children: By Staff Writer

A weekly intelligence briefing tracking the signals shaping business, media, technology, and consumer behaviour across Africa. Created by dentsu Africa's network of experts across the continent, Pulse helps organisations understand what is changing, why it matters and where opportunity lies next.

Africa is often described as a market to watch. The reality is different. Across commerce, media and connectivity, African consumers are building behaviours that global markets are only beginning to understand.
Here are five signals worth paying attention to this week.
1. Commerce is moving into conversations

Consumers across African markets are increasingly discovering products, asking questions, and making purchase decisions within social platforms, creator communities, and messaging environments rather than traditional web journeys.
Africa implication
Africa's mobile first consumer journey is accelerating the shift towards conversational commerce. Discovery, consideration, and purchase are increasingly happening within the same ecosystem.
Opportunity
Brands should design customer experiences around conversations, not websites. The winning brands will be those present where decisions are already being made.
2. Retail media is becoming a growth engine

Retail media continues to gain momentum as retailers strengthen their data capabilities and advertisers seek more measurable routes to conversion. African commerce ecosystems are increasingly being shaped by mobile marketplaces, first party data and integrated shopping experiences.
Africa implication
Africa is not simply adopting global retail media models. It is building its own version, shaped by mobile behaviour, marketplace ecosystems, and social commerce.
Opportunity
Brands should think beyond media buying and focus on connecting audience intelligence, commerce, and measurement into a single growth strategy.
Keep on your radar
Retail media grows up.

MMA South Africa has launched a new retail media measurement framework covering data quality, ROAS, attribution and incrementality. Developed by the MMA South Africa Retail Media Task Force, the framework introduces common measurement standards and begins a 60-day industry consultation alongside a new retail media landscape report and measurement glossary. Its launch signals a market moving beyond experimentation towards accountability, transparency, and measurable business outcomes. Brands should prepare for a future where retail media investment is increasingly tied to standardised performance measurement.
3. East Africa's creative influence continues to grow

Recent leadership investments across East Africa reinforce the region's growing reputation as a centre of creative excellence and culturally relevant storytelling. African creativity is gaining recognition well beyond the continent.
Africa implication
Global brands increasingly need ideas rooted in culture, not simply adapted for it. East Africa continues to emerge as one of the continent's most influential creative hubs.
Opportunity
Brands looking for relevance should invest in local insight, local talent, and local storytelling from the outset.
4. AI is scaling execution, but human understanding remains the advantage

AI continues to reshape media, planning and marketing operations globally. At the same time, understanding people, communities and culture remain the factor that separates effective marketing from efficient marketing.
Africa implication
As technology becomes more accessible, competitive advantage shifts towards deeper audience understanding and cultural intelligence.
Opportunity
Organisations should focus on combining automation with human insight rather than treating them as separate capabilities.
5. Africa's digital economy continues to outpace perceptions
From fintech and payments to social commerce and digital discovery, African consumers continue to adopt behaviours that often leapfrog traditional market development patterns.
Africa implication
Africa's growth story is increasingly a digital story. Organisations treating the continent as an 'emerging opportunity' risk underestimating how quickly markets are evolving.
Opportunity
The greatest opportunities may not come from importing global models into Africa, but from understanding what African consumers are already teaching the rest of the world.
Pulse Point
Africa is collapsing traditional pathways. Media, commerce, technology, and culture are converging faster than global markets anticipated.
The brands that win will be those that understand not only what is changing, but what those changes mean for African consumers.
See the signal. Understand the implication. Act with confidence.
Dentsu Africa helps brands turn signals into strategy, and strategy into growth.
